classification.difficultyReason: Requires deriving boundary equations from graph coordinates, choosing the inequality direction from the unshaded region, and distinguishing strict from inclusive boundaries. These are routine linked graph-to-algebra procedures.

content.prompt: State the sets of inequalities which define the **unshaded** region.

spec.description: Unit Cartesian grid with three unwanted half-planes and an unshaded triangular intersection. Source purple and orange distinguish boundaries; the vertical boundary is black.
spec.mathematics: Axes x=-3..6 and y=-3..5. Dashed y=x-2, shaded below; solid x=1, shaded left; solid y=3-x, shaded above.
spec.answerVisibility: The supplied graph is visible in questions; printed blue answer annotations are excluded.

answer.worked:
The ascending boundary passes through $(0,-2)$ and $(2,0)$, so its equation is $y=x-2$. The unshaded region is above this dashed line: $y>x-2$.

The vertical boundary is solid, with the unshaded region to its right: $x\ge1$.

The descending boundary passes through $(0,3)$ and $(3,0)$, so its equation is $y=3-x$. The unshaded region is below this solid line: $y\le3-x$.

spec.description: Three unwanted half-planes surround the unshaded triangle. Purple and orange distinguish the two ascending boundaries; the descending boundary is black.
spec.mathematics: Unit grid x=-6..8 and y=-8..4. Dashed y=2x+1, shaded above; solid y=-x/2+3, shaded above; solid y=2x/3-4, shaded below.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied graph only; printed answer annotations are stored in answer fields.

answer.worked:
The steep ascending line passes through $(0,1)$ and $(1,3)$, giving gradient $2$ and equation $y=2x+1$. The unshaded region is below its dashed boundary: $y<2x+1$.

The descending line passes through $(0,3)$ and $(6,0)$:
$$m=\frac{0-3}{6-0}=-\frac12.$$
The unshaded region is below its solid boundary: $y\le-\frac{x}{2}+3$.

The shallow ascending line passes through $(0,-4)$ and $(6,0)$:
$$m=\frac{0-(-4)}{6-0}=\frac23.$$
The unshaded region is above its solid boundary: $y\ge\frac23x-4$.

answer.worked:
The ascending boundary passes through $(0,-2)$ and $(2,0)$, giving $y=x-2$. The unshaded region is above this dashed line: $y>x-2$.

The descending boundary passes through $(2,8)$ and $(10,0)$, giving $y=10-x$. The unshaded region is below this solid line:
$$\begin{aligned}y&\le10-x\\x+y&\le10.\end{aligned}$$
The unshaded region is to the right of the dashed vertical boundary $x=3$: $x>3$.

answer.worked:
The ascending boundary passes through $(0,1)$ and $(1,3)$, giving $y=2x+1$. The unshaded region is below this dashed line: $y<2x+1$.

The unshaded region is above the dashed horizontal boundary: $y>1$.

The descending boundary has intercepts $(0,7)$ and $(4,0)$:
$$m=\frac{0-7}{4-0}=-\frac74.$$
The unshaded region is above this solid line:
$$\begin{aligned}y&\ge-\frac74x+7\\4y&\ge-7x+28\\7x+4y&\ge28.\end{aligned}$$
